title: How to start learning GenAI: one model, one use case
oneliner: Don't survey everything - pick one model, learn to prompt it, and test it against one business use case.
says: If you are starting with Generative AI, start with one particular model: explore it and learn how to prompt it with data. There are many model families - foundational models, GANs, VAEs - but pick one and see how it solves your business use case. That is the way to start a GenAI career path.
explained: This is the antidote to tutorial-hopping. The field offers an endless buffet - foundation models, GANs, VAEs, diffusion - and sampling everything teaches you the vocabulary of all of it and the skill of none. Depth on one model transfers: prompting, evaluating outputs, and knowing failure modes are skills that carry across models.

The use-case anchor is doing quiet work here. 'See how that model solves your business use case' turns learning into a project with a pass/fail test. You will learn more from one model that fails your use case - and figuring out why - than from five models demoed on toy prompts.
takeaway: One model + one real use case + prompt practice beats surveying every model family. Depth transfers; browsing does not.
